criteria.criterion: QA finding F1 is fixed: starting 1 m or less from the 45 degree ramp at both walk and run speed, the capsule feet never rise above 0.3 m, while the 30 degree ramp, the 0.2 m step at walking speed and the 0.35 m step block all still behave as before; the root cause (autostep, STEP_PROBE, or both) is identified with evidence.
criteria.evidence: The tests 'never climbs the 45 degree ramp from 0.5 m / 1 m away (walk and run)' assert peak feet height < 0.3 m over a 6 s run and pass; the same suite's 30 degree ramp climb, 'climbs a 0.2 m step and is blocked by a 0.35 m step', snap-to-ground and wall tests still pass (21/21). Root cause: neither autostep nor STEP_PROBE. With STEP_PROBE disabled, with autostep disabled, and with both disabled, the old code still climbs the 45 degree ramp (6/6 tests fail in each variant). Rapier's setMaxSlopeClimbAngle is not enforced for the mostly horizontal movement with a slight downward stick; I did not isolate it further inside Rapier. The fix is in player.ts: limitSlopeClimb drops any rise over a contact steeper than the 40 degree limit (and under 80 degrees, so walls and step risers do not count) once it exceeds stepHeight above the last walkable ground, and slides the horizontal movement along the surface; the stepHeight allowance lets the capsule roll over step edges. One honest limit: the 2 m start in the full test arena is blocked by the arena wall, so the 2 m case also runs on a ramp-only layout (the same ramp-45 block and ground) to prove the ramp itself.

criteria.criterion: QA finding F2 is fixed: the ramp test asserts the peak feet height over the whole run from start positions at 0.5 m, 1 m and 2 m for walk and run, and the report shows the new test failing on the pre-fix code (red) and passing after the fix (green).
criteria.evidence: Six tests (0.5, 1, 2 m x walk, run) track max feet height every tick for 6 s and also assert z < 2.4 (stayed at the foot). criteria.criterion: Jumping, walking off a ledge, and dropping from a height play take-off, a looping fall after the configured air-time threshold, and a hard landing on touchdown when the fall exceeded the hard-landing threshold (soft landing otherwise), with animator.test.ts covering every new transition and threshold; the idle clip is used when standing still.
criteria.evidence: FIRST_PLAY_CLIPS now loads all six clips. animator.test.ts covers: jump on jumpedThisStep, jump to fall at vy <= 0, fall from walk, run and idle only at airTime >= fallDelay (0.15 s, boundary at -0.01 and exact), a hard landing at impactSpeed >= hardLandSpeed from both jump and fall, a soft landing by speed below it, no landing decision while airborne, a normal jump (impact 6.0 m/s) soft versus a 1.3 m drop (7.2 m/s) hard, a ledge-walk-to-hard-landing sequence, and a full animator run with all six clips (standing still stays idle, jump, fall, soft land to idle, walk off a ledge, fall, hard land). Design change to flag: the hard-landing guard moved from airTime >= 0.35 s to impactSpeed >= 6.5 m/s (about a 1.06 m drop). With airTime, every normal 0.6 s jump would have played the 2 s hard landing. The motor now exposes MotorState.impactSpeed, held until the next airborne step so a multi-step frame cannot lose it; GameScene copies it into the animator frame. Not exercised in a browser: the hard landing visual (no drop above 1.06 m was driven); jump frames were smoke-checked.

assumptions: The FBX Mixamo rest poses differ from the avatar's by up to about 26 degrees on some joints (Neck, Arm, Head), the same class of mismatch the design accepted for rotation retargeting; the smoke screenshots showed natural poses, so no rest-delta correction was added.

Avatar scale for the speed measurement is the avatar pelvis-to-foot height (0.896 m) over the FBX pelvis-to-foot height; the walk root-motion speed (1.675 m/s) is higher than the foot-contact figure (1.535 m/s), and the foot-contact number was used.
The Jump clip is trimmed to source frames 21 to 39 (push-off to touchdown, 0.6 s, matching the 0.6 s physics jump) because the motor leaves the ground instantly and the source has 0.5 s of crouch.
Hard Landing leaves the land state at 0.6 of its 2 s duration (1.2 s) per the existing design guard; the player can move during that time, and only running (>= 2.6 m/s) exits early.
The 2 m ramp start needs a ramp-only layout in the test because the arena wall overlaps that approach.
decisionsProposed: Slope limit is enforced in the motor (limitSlopeClimb), not by Rapier's setMaxSlopeClimbAngle, which does not block a 45 degree ramp under the downward stick movement; add as an addendum to ADR-001.

Hard landing is triggered by touchdown impact speed (MotorState.impactSpeed >= ANIMATION.hardLandSpeed 6.5 m/s, about a 1.06 m drop), replacing hardLandAirTime 0.35 s; update design section 5.3 accordingly.
Walk and run clips ship from the new Walking and Running FBX; MOVEMENT is back at 2.2 and 4.8 m/s, superseding the M1 R1 retune (1.6 and 3.8); addendum to ADR-003.
strip-clips.mjs reads FBX with FBXLoader and shifts trimmed loop clips by one frame so clip duration equals the loop period; one-shot clips can be range-trimmed (jump).
lessonsProposed: A test for a blocking behaviour must assert the peak over the whole run from several start offsets; an end-state assertion passes if the character climbs and steps off.

Prove a red test by running it against git show of the old file in a temp copy; prove a root cause by disabling each suspected mechanism on the old code, which here showed that neither suspect was the cause.
